title: Shift the burden

readouts.l: Consumers' share of each unit's tax

predict.q: Start: a tax of $1.50 per unit, PED −1, PES 2, so consumers bear 2/3 of each unit's tax. Demand becomes much less elastic (PED −0.25), with the same tax and supply. What happens to the consumers' share?

options.fb: Less elastic demand: buyers keep buying, so sellers pass on more of the tax. The consumers' share rises from 2/3 to 8/9.
Less elastic demand means buyers can't avoid the tax by switching, so sellers can raise the price more: the consumers' share rises.

options.s: It stays at 2/3, because the tax per unit has not changed
options.fb: The tax per unit fixes the total gap, not how it is split. The split follows the elasticities.

task: Move the **Demand elasticity** slider to −0.25 and watch Pc, Pp and the two shaded burdens.

target.do: Move the Demand elasticity slider to −0.25 (keep the tax at $1.50 and PES at 2), then press Check.
target.hint: Set Demand elasticity to −0.25, with the tax at $1.50 and PES at 2.

takeaway: Less elastic demand → consumers bear a bigger share (here 8/9), and quantity falls less.
explore: Now try the other sliders: which side bears more when supply is the less elastic side?
alt: Tax incidence diagram: demand D, supply S and S plus tax, with the consumers' and producers' burdens shaded.
